correctness.rationale: The Euclidean strip is a convex universal cover with a glide-reflection deck group. Minimization across exhaustive parity classes gives exactly \(\min\{u,\sqrt{(a-u)^2+4b^2}\}\). The shorter boundary separation is uniform on [0,a]; exact integration of both monotone branches proves the complete CDF, its integrable threshold singularity, and all zero/positive threshold boundaries. Recovering a from the small-radius slope and b from the support endpoint establishes the full inverse equivalence classes. The independent standard-library checker verifies 210,000 deck-pair distances, 68 integrated CDF cases, and seven analytic means; finite checks are corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: The boundary-distance probability distribution is a natural metric-measure invariant and an observable for partial or unlabeled boundary inverse problems. The exact formula exhibits a canonical square-root density singularity and, more substantively, a sharp aspect-ratio cutoff at which the full boundary distance metric loses all information about transverse width. For narrower bands the histogram alone reconstructs both geometric parameters. This complete classification of a natural two-parameter nonorientable flat family is more than a special numerical tabulation; it gives an exact identifiability boundary alongside classic lens-rigidity results.
